rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith can grow or diminish; its changeability is why God tests people.
rows.anchor: faith is something which is liable to increase and decrease; had it been something static, there would have been no need to test it

rows.speaker: Abū Ḥanīfah
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah is said to deny that faith increases or decreases; Islahi says this view concerns legal faith and is correct in that context.
rows.anchor: If it is ascribed to Im ām Abū Ḥanīfah that he was not convinced of the fact

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal terms, every Muslim believer has equal faith and receives equal civic standing in an Islamic state.
rows.anchor: As far as faith in the legal sense is concerned, it is found in equal extent in all Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife rank depends on each person's actual faith, which only God knows and will judge.
rows.anchor: the matter there depends on the actual faith found in a person – something known only to God and He alone will decide about it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's urging believers to accompany the Prophet is a favor that strengthens their faith and opens a path to reward.
rows.anchor: He actually did a favour to them so that by doing this virtuous act they could further enhance their faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no assistance: all heavenly and earthly forces are under His control, and He can punish disbelievers through them.
rows.anchor: All the forces of the heavens and the earth are in the control of the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about admission to Paradise is a permutative (badal) explanation of the preceding purpose of growing believers' faith.
rows.anchor: the linguistic style adopted is permutative ( badal)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's strengthening of believers' inner radiance aims to admit believing men and women to eternal gardens and remove their sins, a great triumph.
rows.anchor: He wants believing men and women to enter into gardens watered by streams; they will abide therein forever and He will remove all their sins

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Paradise is named before sins are erased, the order is only apparent: cleansing precedes admission, while Paradise comes first to foreground glad tidings.
rows.anchor: In order to highlight the aspect of glad tidings, Paradise is mentioned first

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of this as supreme success introduces the hypocrites, who thought staying home spared them danger but had actually exposed themselves to it.
rows.anchor: these words are a prelude to the mention of the Hypocrites whose mention is coming up

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same trial that opens a path to great success for Muslims exposes the blemishes of hypocrites and idolaters, conclusively conveying the truth and bringing them toward doom.
rows.anchor: their blemishes are fully exposed and the truth is conclusively conveyed to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil thoughts named here refer to the hypocrites' expectation in 48:12 that the Messenger and his companions would never return.
rows.anchor: refer to those evil thoughts of the Hypocrites which are mentioned ahead in verse 12

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrisy resembles polytheism because both break a claimed pledge to God; the Qur’an groups hypocrites with idolaters and indicates their similar fate.
rows.anchor: Because of this similarity, the Qur’ān has likened hypocrisy to polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical phrase means the misfortune hypocrites wished for Muslims will instead befall them, along with those on whom they pinned hopes.
rows.anchor: they are waiting for misfortunes to befall the Muslims even though these misfortunes are going to befall them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women are named alongside men because, during trials, wives and children can help foster hypocrisy; the excuse in 48:11 about goods and families illustrates this influence.
rows.anchor: if hypocrisy is nurtured in a group, then the wife and children have a great role in this

rows.speaker: Prophet (sws)
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says children can push a person toward miserliness and cowardice; Islahi cites it as evidence of family influence in trials.
rows.anchor: A Ḥadīth of the Prophet (sws) also bears witness to this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, a faithful person's wife's and children's perseverance and trust in God can help faith take firm root.
rows.anchor: the determination and perseverance of his wife and children and their trust in God have a great role

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning women on both sides makes clear that God knows believing women's sacrifices and hypocritical women's worldly indolence.
rows.anchor: neither is their Lord unaware of the sacrifices of the believing women nor of the attitude of indolence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated reference to God's legions here expresses disgust and disavowal toward hypocrites: if they choose Hell, their absence is no loss to God.
rows.anchor: if they want to become the fuel of Hell, then may do so; it would only be good riddance

none: Bare sūrah heading and page apparatus; no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Makkan idols are inventions of fancy without reality or divine sanction; reason, instinct, and intellect cannot affirm them.
rows.anchor: their false idols, on the basis of which they are denying the warnings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters follow conjecture and baseless wishes despite manifest guidance; desire cannot replace truth, and they will face the warned facts rather than what they wish for.
rows.anchor: conjectures and suppositions cannot take the place of truth, and false wishes and desires have no basis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels cannot intercede without God's permission; belief in angelic daughters and intercession as escape from accountability is fanciful and futile.
rows.anchor: The Almighty alone shall give permission to intercede to whom He wants and for whom He chooses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is consoled to turn from worldly people indifferent to God's message; God knows who strays or is guided and will give each person their due.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) has been solaced that he should turn away from the slaves to this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God controls the heavens and earth; those who avoid grave sins and indecencies, though they may commit minor sins without persisting, will receive His ample mercy.
rows.anchor: only those shall be rewarded in the Hereafter who used to abstain from heinous sins and open indecencies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
rows.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet saw the angel in the higher horizon and again near the farthest lote-tree; Islahi says this could not be a product of fancy.
rows.anchor: There is absolutely no possibility that this observation which he has stated to them be a product of his fancy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel taught the Prophet like an affectionate teacher, approaching and bending over his pupil, and the Prophet fully grasped the instruction rather than hearing unclear distant words.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) fully grasped and understood this instruction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Makkan adversaries cannot rely on self-claimed deities to escape fear of Judgment: Lāt, Manāt, and ʿUzzā are merely hypothetical names without real-world referents.
rows.anchor: they are merely hypothetical names which qualify no one in the real world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward and punishment are realities, and conjecture or wishes cannot overcome them; all affairs of heaven and earth remain in God's hands.
rows.anchor: Reward and punishment is a reality. They cannot combat reality with conjecture

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels cannot speak or intercede without God's permission; naming them as female and relying on them to evade accountability will not help, for God knows the righteous and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: Not even an angel can open his mouth in the presence of God without His permission
